long_biography.plain_text:
Tatlıcı entered business through a family group created by his father, Şeyhmus Tatlıcı, and was among the founders of Şe-Tat Mining. He also held a documented stake in a family securities business. After his father died, the siblings selected him to head the group, a role he held until leaving management.

Beyond the inherited platform, Tatlıcı developed separately owned mining interests including Motat Mining, 5 M Mining and Bursa Krom. Those businesses focus on mineral extraction and related investment. He also briefly co-owned Istanbul gallery Galerist with architect Melkan Tabanlıoğlu and later joined the group of patrons that funded a permanent home for Turkey’s pavilion at the Venice Biennale.

uncertainties.detail: The authoritative input assigns person 2134 to the exact 40-metre, 246-GT Baraka from 2008. SuperYacht Times independently confirms the vessel but withholds its owner. Contemporary Turkish reporting instead says the 40-metre Baraka belonged to father Şeyhmuz Tatlıcı, while naming Taha as owner of a different yacht and distinguishing younger brother Şeyhmuz. This appears to be a family-level attribution error or later relationship change; no Baraka fact is used to infer Taha's business or wealth.

The canonical upstream form Taha Tatlıcı is preserved. Regulatory documents often render the surname as TATLICI or Tatlici because Turkish dotless-ı characters are omitted. Exact company, father, Istanbul and yachting anchors establish that these forms refer to the same person. Father Şeyhmus Tatlıcı and a younger family member also named Şeyhmuz remain separate.

Şe-Tat and the broader Tatlıcı estate include numerous heirs and historically spanned construction, property and mining. Only Taha's stated 11% Şe-Tat stake, his management period and companies explicitly registered to him are attributed personally. Family real estate, siblings' holdings and undivided estate values are not treated as his assets.

Tatlıcı left management of the family group in 2016. His representative identified three mining companies registered to him in 2019, and 2023 reporting identifies him as Motat Mining's owner. Private-company production, current titles and asset values are not disclosed. Metals & Mining is therefore well supported as the current principal identifiable sector, but not as a complete balance-sheet description.

A 2023 article reported Tatlıcı as age 53, implying a 1969 or 1970 birth depending on birthday, while current public biographies explicitly acknowledge the absence of a verified date. No birth day, month, year or place is proposed. Existing Turkey birth country is retained without expansion to a city or family-origin inference.

No dedicated Forbes profile or exact-person Forbes article was found. Searches for LinkedIn, Instagram and a personal website did not produce a strong, verified exact-person account; entertainment and yacht photographs are not proposed as profiles.

The approved catalogue has no generic Metals & Mining, chromium-mining or olivine-mining tag. Nickel, coal, gold, copper and iron-ore tags would overstate or misclassify the documented operations, while art-collector tags require a notable collection rather than gallery ownership or sponsorship. No tag is proposed and no closed-world candidate is created.

The biographies exclude the Baraka conflict, vessel purchases and prices, current relationship coverage, inheritance litigation and unverified wealth estimates. The family succession is included only to explain the durable mixed wealth origin and later independent operating platform.
